<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Davis |first1=Tristan J. |last2=García |first2=Gonzalo Juárez |date=2025-01-17 |title=A New Species of Beschorneria Kunth from Central Mexico and a Reassessment of Beschorneria calcicola García-Mend. |url=https://bioone.org/journals/haseltonia/volume-32/issue-1/026.032.0102/A-New-Species-of-Beschorneria-Kunth-from-Central-Mexico-and/10.2985/026.032.0102.full |journal=Haseltonia |volume=32 |issue=1 |doi=10.2985/026.032.0102 |issn=1070-0048|url-access=subscription }}</ref>'''Beschorneria''' is a [[genus]] of [[succulent plant]]s belonging to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]], subfamily [[Agavoideae]],<ref>{{citation |last=Stevens |first=P.F.  |title=Angiosperm Phylogeny Website: Asparagales: Agavoideae |url=http://www.mobot.org/mobot/research/apweb/orders/asparagalesweb.htm#Agavaceae }}</ref> [[native plant|native]] to semi-arid areas of [[Mexico]] and [[Central America]].<ref name=marta>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=300550 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> They are generally large [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennials]] forming clumps of grey-green leaves, with tall flower-spikes to {{convert|1.5|m|ft}}. Marginally [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]], they may require winter protection in areas subject to frost.

Three names have been coined using the name ''Beschorneria (B. floribunda, B. multiflora,'' and ''B. parmentieri),'' all referring to the species now known as ''[[Furcraea parmentieri]]''.<ref name=marta/><ref>García-Mendoza, Abisaí Josué. 2000. Revisión taxonómica de las especies arborescentes de ''Furcraea'' (Agavaceae) en México y Guatemala Boletín de la Sociedad Botánica de México 66: 113–129</ref> See ''[[Furcraea]].''
